mainTopic: Does the time limit (זְמַן) apply to offerings on a private altar (בָּמָה קְטַנָּה)? Closing the sugya and the end of מסכת זבחים.
overview: The גמרא is asking whether the time limit (זְמַן) that disqualifies קדשים on the main altar also applies to offerings on a small private altar (בָּמָה קְטַנָּה). First it tries a קל וחומר from bird offerings: a מום does not disqualify birds, yet time does, so time should surely disqualify a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה, where a מום does disqualify. Then it knocks that argument down. Birds are stricter in another way, because a זר may not offer them, while on a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה a זר may. Since logic fails, the גמרא brings the פסוק "וזאת תורת זבח השלמים". It teaches that the time limit on a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה is the same as on a בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה. The amud ends with the הדרן, closing פרק פרת חטאת and the whole of מסכת זבחים.

steps.title: A logical proof from bird offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a קל וחומר: birds are not disqualified by a מום, yet the time limit disqualifies them. So offerings on a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה, which a מום does disqualify, should surely be disqualified by time too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bird offerings are not disqualified by a blemish, and still the time limit disqualifies them. Offerings of a small private altar are disqualified by a blemish. So shouldn't the time limit disqualify them as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to prove with a קל וחומר that the time limit applies to offerings on a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In one way birds are more lenient: a מום does not disqualify them, yet the time limit still applies to them. A בָּמָה קְטַנָּה is stricter in that same way, since a מום does disqualify its offerings. So the argument says the time limit should apply there all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: A physical blemish that can disqualify an offering
The time limit for an offering; going past it disqualifies the offering
A small private altar, allowed at certain periods in history
A logical argument from a lenient case to a stricter one

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of strictness. Being disqualified by a מום and being disqualified by time are two separate rules. The argument uses the first to prove the second.

phrases.english: which a blemish does not disqualify,
then the offerings of a small altar,
isn't it logical that time disqualifies them?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה עוֹפוֹת, שֶׁאֵין הַמּוּם פּוֹסֵל בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question, raised just before this text, of whether the time limit applies on a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה.
steps.raayaObject: That the time limit disqualifies offerings of a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from bird offerings, which the time limit disqualifies even though a מום does not.

steps.title: Birds are stricter in another way
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is refuted. Birds have their own strictness: a זר (non-כהן) may not offer them. On a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה a זר is allowed to offer, so maybe the time limit doesn't apply there either.
steps.simpleTranslation: But birds are special, because a non-priest may not offer them. On a small altar a non-priest may offer. So maybe there the time limit does not disqualify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is breaking the קל וחומר from step 1 by showing that birds are stricter than a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is lenient in every way that matters. Birds turn out to be strict too, since only a כהן may offer them. A בָּמָה קְטַנָּה is lenient on that point, so maybe it is lenient about time as well. Now the proof from logic is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, allowed (here: allowed to do the offering)
"What about X, which has…": the standard way to knock down a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a ruling that the time limit doesn't apply. It only shows the logical proof is weak, which opens the way for a פסוק.

phrases.english: They are special, since a non-priest is not fit to offer them;
can you say the same about a small altar,
So time should not disqualify there!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְעוֹפוֹת – שֶׁכֵּן אֵין הַזָּר כָּשֵׁר בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the logical proof is rejected, not the conclusion itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Birds have a strictness (no זר may offer them) that a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה lacks, so the comparison fails.

steps.title: A verse makes the small altar like the great altar
steps.stepSummary: Since logic failed, the גמרא brings the פסוק "וזאת תורת זבח השלמים". It teaches that the time limit on a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה is the same as on a בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says: "And this is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings." This makes the time limit of a small altar the same as the time limit of a great altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real source: a פסוק teaching that the time limit applies on a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "תורת זבח השלמים" treat all שלמים as one law, wherever they are offered. So the time limit of the public altar carries over to the private altar. The conclusion of step 1 stands, but now it rests on a פסוק instead of logic.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches": introduces the פסוק that settles the question
The great public altar, the altar of the משכן

steps.whatToRemember: The time limit disqualifies offerings on a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה just as on a בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה. This is learned from "וזאת תורת זבח השלמים", not from the קל וחומר, which was refuted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a קל וחומר is tried and refuted, and then a פסוק proves the very same result.

phrases.english: "And this is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings"
to make the time limit of a small altar
like the time limit of a great altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 2 refutes the קל וחומר of step 1, a פסוק supplies the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the time limit applies on a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 7:11, "וזאת תורת זבח השלמים", which treats all שלמים as one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The time limit of a בָּמָה קְטַנָּה is the same as that of a בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק פרת חטאת and מסכת זבחים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the last פרק, פרת חטאת, and for the whole מסכת זבחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter פרת חטאת, and מסכת זבחים is complete.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line. It ends the chapter פרת חטאת and finishes all of מסכת זבחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הדרן עלך" expresses the hope that we will return to learn this chapter again. "וסליקא לה" announces that the whole מסכת is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": the closing formula of a פרק
"And it is completed": marks the end of a מסכת

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter "The Red Heifer",

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter and the מסכת after the final sugya.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק פרת חטאת and of מסכת זבחים.
